prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the indoor climbing gym layout, showing a flat padded floor, an angled climbing wall rising immediately to the right within 0.5–1.5 metres, and cylindrical rope buckets arranged in a receding row from 1.5 to 8 metres away. In frames 1 and 2, the camera wearer looks down at the mat with a person in a black shirt and harness partly visible at the lower-left edge within arm's reach (under 1 metre), while in frames 3 and 4 the wearer turns and looks up toward two standing people facing each other about 3–4 metres ahead on the left (separated by less than 0.5 metres, within each other's arm's reach) and a seated person 7–8 metres away against the back wall. In frame 5, the camera turns left and tilts down as the person in the black shirt stands directly in front of the wearer at roughly 1 metre, facing and looking toward the camera within arm's reach, with two other people standing 4–5 metres behind them to the upper left and buckets flanking both sides at 1.5–3 metres. The depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouettes of the conversing pair and the row of floor buckets from the cluttered, brightly patterned background walls in frames 3–4, which is harder to gauge in RGB alone. However, it is unreliable on the flat rope coils on the floor (which nearly vanish into the mat plane), misses the climber high on the right wall in frame 3, and saturates to uniform bright white on the close person's head in frame 5 and the upper-right wall overhang in frame 3.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete people and cylindrical rope buckets across the gym floor, though it mislabels the floor buckets as 'cup' and a distant right-edge object in frame 5 as 'skateboard'. It misses everything in frame 1 and most of frame 2 except one bucket at 2 metres and the legs of a person 4 metres ahead at the top-left edge, whereas frames 3 and 4 detect the two standing people facing each other at 3–4 metres on the left (partially occluding smaller background people 5–8 metres behind them), the seated person 7–8 metres away to the right, and near buckets at 1.5–4 metres. As the camera turns left in frame 5, a large mask captures the person in the black shirt standing 1 metre directly in front of and facing the wearer (within arm's reach, legs cut off at the bottom frame edge), alongside two people standing 4–5 metres behind them to the upper left and a cluster of five distant people 6–10 metres away at the upper right. Compared to the busy RGB image, segmentation makes it easier to count and delineate overlapping distant people in the background of frames 3–5. The map is unreliable in omitting the climbing walls, ropes, the close person in frames 1–2, the climber high on the wall in frame 3, and most of the floor buckets, while assigning incorrect object classes to the buckets it does detect.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D body and hand skeletons on a black background, detecting only a single person in frames 1, 4, and 5 while leaving frames 2 and 3 completely empty. In frame 1, an inverted, distorted yellow skeleton at the lower left corresponds to the partly visible person within 1 metre of the camera wearer, whereas in frame 4 a yellow skeleton captures only the left-side standing person (about 3.5 metres away, turned in right profile toward their partner within arm's reach, with their lower legs occluded by a bucket). In frame 5, as the camera faces the person in the black shirt standing 1 metre away, a frontal yellow torso-and-leg skeleton with magenta hand keypoints shows them facing and looking directly toward the camera wearer, with both hands lowered to hip level holding the rope within arm's reach of both themselves and the wearer. The magenta hand skeletons in frame 5 make the exact articulation and position of both hands gripping the rope near the harness much clearer than in the dark RGB regions. However, the map is highly unreliable across the sequence, failing to detect any people in frames 2 and 3 (including the climber on the wall and the foreground pair), missing the second standing person in frame 4 and all background people in frames 3–5, and hallucinating an upside-down torso structure on the cropped person in frame 1.
